voiceGuide: Guide the child through four biomes: Forest, Desert, Ocean, and Arctic. Read every quiz question aloud, then read each answer choice aloud, and finally read the fun fact after a correct answer. Use an encouraging, adventurous tone.

welcome.text: Welcome, explorer! Help animals find their home!

wrong_1.text: Hmm, try again! Think about where this animal lives.

wrong_2.text: Not quite! You can do it!

biome_complete.text: Wow! You explored the whole area!

all_done.text: You explored every biome! Amazing work!

q_forest_1.text: An owl sleeps during the bright day. Where is the safest place for them to hide?

q_forest_1_a.text: A hollow hole inside a tree trunk

q_forest_1_c.text: On top of an open, sunny flower

fact_forest_1.text: Spotted owls sleep inside dark hollow trees. Their brown feathers blend in with the bark to keep them safe from danger!

q_forest_2.text: Squirrels need food to survive the cold winter. What do they harvest and store in the autumn?

fact_forest_2.text: Squirrels hide thousands of nuts in secret places under the ground. The nuts they forget grow into beautiful new trees!

q_forest_3.text: Grizzly bears must eat a lot of food before their long winter sleep. What is their favorite meal?

q_forest_3_a.text: Fresh river fish and sweet honey

fact_forest_3.text: Grizzly bears eat lots of fat-rich salmon and wild berries to grow strong before sleeping all through the snowy winter!

q_desert_1.text: A camel travels over very hot sand dunes. Where do they store fuel when food is hard to find?

fact_desert_1.text: A camel's hump is full of fat. When food is scarce, their body turns that fat into energy to help them walk for many days.

q_desert_2.text: The desert sun is super hot during the day. How does a little lizard stay nice and cool?

q_desert_2_a.text: Hiding deep under the cool sand

q_desert_2_b.text: Climbing up a pine tree branch

fact_desert_2.text: Desert lizards crawl into underground holes to rest during the hottest hours, and do a little dance to lift their toes off the hot sand!

q_desert_3.text: A scorpion hunts bugs in the dark desert night. How do they find food without bright light?

q_desert_3_a.text: Using sensitive hairs to feel steps

q_desert_3_c.text: Tasting dry sand on the wind

fact_desert_3.text: Scorpions have tiny hairs on their legs that feel bug footsteps in the sand. They also glow bright blue under the moonlight!

q_ocean_1.text: Little clownfish need a safe place to live. Where is the best spot for them to hide?

fact_ocean_1.text: Clownfish live safely inside stinging sea anemones. Their special slimy skin shields them from the anemone's stings!

q_ocean_2.text: An octopus has no bones. What do they do to escape from a big hungry shark?

q_ocean_2_a.text: Shoot a cloud of dark ink

q_ocean_2_b.text: Sing a loud song to make friends

q_ocean_2_c.text: Hide inside a giant clam shell

fact_ocean_2.text: An octopus shoots ink to confuse predators and can change their skin color in an instant to blend in with ocean rocks!

q_ocean_3.text: Sharks must keep moving through the deep sea. Why is swimming constantly so important?

q_ocean_3_a.text: To push fresh water through gills

q_ocean_3_b.text: To keep their muscular fins warm

fact_ocean_3.text: Many sharks must swim day and night. Moving forward keeps water flowing across their gills so they can breathe while resting!

q_arctic_1.text: Polar bears live in freezing blizzards. How do they stay warm in the ice and snow?

q_arctic_1_a.text: Thick fat and clear hollow fur

q_arctic_1_b.text: Drinking hot cocoa by a campfire

fact_arctic_1.text: Polar bear fur isn't actually white! Their hair is clear and hollow, trapping the warm sunshine right against their black skin.

q_arctic_2.text: Father penguins look after their single egg in the winter. How do they keep it cozy?

q_arctic_2_a.text: Cradling the egg on warm feet

q_arctic_2_b.text: Building a nest with dry mud

q_arctic_2_c.text: Hanging the egg from cold ice

fact_arctic_2.text: Penguin fathers balance the egg on top of their feet under a warm belly flap to shield it from freezing winds.

q_arctic_3.text: Reindeer look for food deep under heavy winter snow. What helps them dig through the ice?

fact_arctic_3.text: Reindeer have wide, scoop-shaped hooves that act like snow shovels to dig up tasty plants hidden deep under the winter snow!
